rules.title: Structural stability of evacuation-supporting portions in CVFPP areas
rules.intent: Ensure portions of buildings supporting evacuation locations resist flood-induced flotation, collapse and lateral movement during a 200-year flood event in areas protected by the Central Valley Flood Protection Plan.
evidence_required: Construction documents showing WSEL200 and floor/roof elevations (per AY101.1)
Hydrostatic load calculations per ASCE 7 Chapter 5 referencing depth from WSEL200
Structural drawings of anchorage and load path for evacuation-supporting portions
If using flood vents under exception, drawings showing minimum one vent on two opposite sides per Figure AY103
Registered design professional stamp where automatic-entry openings, valves or yield panels are used

rules.title: Use of defined terms and fallback meanings
rules.intent: Establish that defined terms govern code interpretation and provide an authoritative fallback to the California Building Standards Code (and Webster's for SFM applications) when terms are not defined.
evidence_required: Construction documents and specifications using terms consistent with Chapter 2 definitions
For SFM-regulated occupancies under Section 1.11, references documenting Webster's Third fallback when applicable

rules.title: Complete load path for all prescribed loads
rules.intent: Require buildings to safely support all prescribed loads with a complete load path from origin to foundation so prescriptive construction is presumed compliant.
evidence_required: Structural plans showing continuous load path from roof to foundation
Load schedules listing dead, live, roof, flood, snow, wind and seismic loads applicable to the project
Indication of which prescriptive provisions are being used (or engineered design package per R301.1.3)
Climatic and geographic design criteria filled in per Table R301.2

rules.title: Permitted alternative prescriptive standards to R301
rules.intent: Allow specific industry standards (WFCM, AISI S230, ICC 400) as alternatives to R301 prescriptive provisions, with engineered portions referred to the California Building Code.
evidence_required: Designation of which alternative standard (WFCM, AISI S230, or ICC 400) governs the design
Cross-reference table demonstrating compliance with the chosen standard's limits
If engineering supplements the prescriptive standard, engineered calculations per California Building Code stamped by a California-licensed design professional
Identification of any provisions of this code that still apply to elements outside the chosen standard

rules.title: Engineered design required for elements exceeding prescriptive limits
rules.intent: Require accepted engineering practice (and California-licensed architect/engineer stamp where amended) for any structural element that exceeds R301 prescriptive limits or otherwise does not conform to the code.

california_amendments.statutory_basis: Business and Professions Code Sections 5537 and 6737.1

evidence_required: Engineering calculations and structural drawings stamped by a California-licensed architect or engineer for the nonconforming portion
Identification of which elements exceed R301 prescriptive limits and the basis for engineered design
Demonstration that engineered elements are compatible with the surrounding conventional framing
For woodframe dwellings >2 stories + basement, complete stamped construction documents
For cold-formed steel, concrete, masonry, or SIP buildings, stamped floor/wall/roof-ceiling structural drawings

rules.title: Intermodal shipping containers as buildings
rules.intent: Direct designers of repurposed intermodal shipping containers to the structural provisions of the California Building Code rather than CRC prescriptive provisions.
evidence_required: Structural calculations and drawings demonstrating compliance with CBC Section 3115
Identification of container origin, size, and modification details (cuts, openings, reinforcements)
California-licensed architect or engineer stamp on container structural design
Connection details for stacking, anchorage, and load path to foundation

rules.title: Wind design required where prescriptive wind provisions do not apply
rules.intent: Require an engineered wind design (using one of the listed methods) wherever Figure R301.2.1.1 mandates wind design or where the ultimate design wind speed in a special wind region equals or exceeds 140 mph.

must_use_one_of: ICC Standard for Residential Construction in High-Wind Regions (ICC 600)
ASCE 7 Minimum Design Loads for Buildings and Other Structures
AISI Standard for Cold-Formed Steel Framing - Prescriptive Method (AISI S230)

evidence_required: Identification of ultimate design wind speed Vult and whether the site is in a special wind region
Indication of which Figure R301.2.1.1 region applies
Wind design package using one of the five permitted methods (WFCM, ICC 600, ASCE 7, AISI S230, or CBC)
Stamped calculations by a California-licensed engineer for engineered wind designs
Schedule of components and cladding pressures for wall coverings, windows, doors, garage doors and skylights

rules.title: Protection of openings in windborne debris regions
rules.intent: Require glazed exterior openings in windborne debris regions to be protected against impact and pressure to keep the building envelope intact during high-wind events.

glazing_protection_must_meet: Large Missile Test of ASTM E1886
ASTM E1996 as modified in Section R301.2.1.2.1

evidence_required: Designation that the project site is in a windborne debris region (per Table R301.2 footnote m and Figure R301.2(2))
Test reports showing glazed openings comply with ASTM E1886 (Large Missile) and ASTM E1996
For garage doors with glazing, ANSI/DASMA 115 or approved impact-resistance test report
If wood structural panel exception is used: panel thickness, span, precut/predrilled detail, attachment hardware schedule, and Vult/mean roof height calculations
Component and cladding pressure calculations per Table R301.2.1(1) or ASCE 7

rules.title: Use actual material weights for dead load
rules.intent: Require dead load determination to use actual material weights and account for fixed service equipment so the structure is not under-designed for self-weight.
evidence_required: Dead load schedule listing each assembly (roof, floors, walls, partitions) with material weights
Inventory of fixed service equipment (HVAC units, water heaters, solar arrays, etc.) and their weights included in dead load
Manufacturer data sheets supporting equipment weights
Structural calculations showing dead load values used in member sizing

rules.title: Minimum uniformly distributed live loads
rules.intent: Require structural members to be designed for at least the minimum uniformly distributed live loads in Table R301.5 to ensure adequate occupant and use-load capacity.
evidence_required: Live load schedule per occupancy/use that references Table R301.5 values
Member sizing calculations using the tabulated live loads
Verification of stair tread capacity for the 300-lb concentrated load on a 2x2 area
Verification of elevated garage floor capacity for the 2,000-lb concentrated load on a 4.5x4.5 area
Identification of attic live load category (with or without storage) and corresponding load

rules.title: Under-floor space moisture control
rules.intent: Prevent moisture damage and decay in crawl spaces by requiring either ventilation (R408.2) or unvented-with-controls construction (R408.3), plus access, debris removal, grading, flood resistance and a vapor retarder where applicable.

requires.ventilation_minimum_net_area_ratio: 1 sq ft per 150 sq ft of under-floor area (or 1/1500 with Class I vapor retarder over ground)

evidence_required: Crawl-space ventilation calculation showing net area >= 1/150 (or 1/1500 with Class I vapor retarder) of under-floor area
Plan showing ventilation openings within 3 ft of each external corner (or cross-ventilation layout when vapor retarder is used)
If unvented: Class I vapor retarder spec, mechanical exhaust/conditioned-supply/plenum/dehumidification design
Access opening dimensions on plans (>= 18x24 in floor or 16x24 in wall) and areaway detail where below grade
For flood hazard areas: flood opening details per R322.2.2 and grading sections showing under-floor grade vs outside finished grade

rules.title: Floor construction must accommodate and transmit Section R301 loads
rules.intent: Ensure all floors (including attic-equipment-supporting floors) are designed to carry and transfer R301 loads to the supporting structure.
evidence_required: Floor framing plans with member sizes, spans and spacings
Load takedown showing R301 loads carried by each floor and transferred to supporting walls/beams/foundations
Identification of attic spaces housing mechanical/plumbing equipment with corresponding floor design
Connection details transmitting loads to supporting structural elements

rules.title: Wood floor framing materials must be identified and conform to standards
rules.intent: Ensure wood and wood-based products used for load-supporting floor framing are identifiable, traceable to recognized standards, and of established structural capacity.
evidence_required: Lumber grade marks visible on submitted samples or specified in construction documents
Manufacturer specifications and ICC-ES or equivalent reports for prefabricated I-joists, glulam, SCL, CLT and rim boards
ANSI/APA, ASTM and DOC PS 20 references in the wood material schedule
For preservative-treated members, identification per R317.2
For end-jointed lumber in fire-resistance-rated assemblies, HRA designation in grade mark

rules.title: Draftstopping required in floor assemblies
rules.intent: Require draftstopping in floor framing per R302.12 to limit concealed-space air movement that could spread fire or smoke.
evidence_required: Floor framing plans showing draftstop locations and continuity per R302.12
Specification of draftstop materials (e.g., 1/2-in gypsum, 3/8-in wood structural panel, or other approved materials) per R302.12
Section details showing draftstop full-depth integration with framing
Coordination with fireblocking per R502.13/R302.11 at penetrations

rules.title: Windborne debris protection of windows, glass doors and doors with glass
rules.intent: Require fenestration in windborne debris regions to be protected by tested-and-labeled assemblies or impact-protective systems so the building envelope remains intact during high-wind events.

impact_protective_systems.design_wind_pressure_basis: Table R301.2.1(1) adjusted by Table R301.2.1(2) or ASCE 7 (with optional 0.6 multiplier when ASCE 7 used)

evidence_required: Test reports for fenestration to ASTM E1886 + ASTM E1996 (or AAMA 506) from approved independent laboratory
Labels on installed fenestration showing manufacturer, performance characteristics, and approved inspection agency
For impact protective systems: ASTM E1886/E1996 impact reports plus ASTM E330 design wind pressure reports
Design wind pressure calculations per Table R301.2.1(1) adjusted by R301.2.1(2) or per ASCE 7 (with 0.6 multiplier documentation if used)
Permanent (non-removable) label evidence on impact protective systems
